title: Gibson assembly: GFP into pUC19
summary: Open pUC19 by PCR across 395-452, amplify GFP with the overlap at each junction carried as a primer tail, join the 2 fragments in one NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix reaction, and confirm the clone by colony PCR and sequencing.

overview.Assembly: NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix, 50 °C for 15 min

highlights: One reaction joins 2 fragments: pUC19 backbone (2629 bp) and GFP (717 bp).
pUC19 backbone and GFP share 16 bp at 380, taken from pUC19 backbone and carried by the other as a primer tail.
GFP and pUC19 backbone share 16 bp at 1113, taken from pUC19 backbone and carried by the other as a primer tail.
GFP reads on the opposite strand from lac promoter, 60 bp away, so that promoter does not transcribe it.
There is no ribosome binding site annotated ahead of GFP, so the clone is not expected to make its protein.
The insertion interrupts lacZα, so correct clones are white and empty vector is blue on X-gal and IPTG.

checks.name: junctions
checks.detail: 16 bp at 380, from pUC19 backbone, 16 bp at 1113, from pUC19 backbone

checks.name: overlap length
checks.detail: pUC19 backbone-GFP 16 bp, GFP-pUC19 backbone 16 bp; NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix documents 15-20 bp here and calls 12 bp the shortest that works at all

checks.name: overlap tm
checks.detail: pUC19 backbone-GFP 48 °C, GFP-pUC19 backbone 48 °C; by the Wallace rule, against a floor of 48 °C

checks.name: overlap gc
checks.detail: pUC19 backbone-GFP 50%, GFP-pUC19 backbone 50%; no source quantifies a GC band for an overlap, so nothing judges this

checks.name: overlap hairpin
checks.detail: pUC19 backbone-GFP 4 bp, GFP-pUC19 backbone 4 bp; a highly palindromic overlap costs NEB up to tenfold fewer colonies; 10 bases reading the same on both strands is this package's floor

checks.name: overlap repeat
checks.detail: pUC19 backbone-GFP 0 bp, GFP-pUC19 backbone 0 bp; both NEB manuals refuse a repeating sequence at an overlap's end and ask for 2 bases of anything else outside it

checks.name: overlap similarity
checks.detail: pUC19 backbone-GFP and GFP-pUC19 backbone share 3 bases, the most any two here do; NEB asks for a unique overlap at each junction but nobody quantifies how alike is too alike, so nothing judges this

checks.name: fragment count
checks.detail: 1 insert in one reaction; New England Biolabs recommends 5 or fewer for NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix

checks.name: assembly DNA
checks.detail: 0.0927 pmol in 20 µL; NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix takes 0.03-0.2 pmol at this fragment count

checks.name: primers
checks.detail: 9 designed, 3 with a warning, 0 failing: GC on 2, Tm on 1; not judged: full-primer Tm, 3' end stability

steps.title: Amplify pUC19 backbone
instructions: Thaw the buffer, dNTPs and primers on ice, then vortex and spin them down.
Mix the master mix, dispense it into each tube, then add the pUC19 template.
Run the program below: 64.1 °C annealing and 60 s extension for a 2629 bp product.
notes: Its primers carry no tail: neither of its junctions is this fragment's to carry.
The annealing temperature above is read from the annealing regions alone; a tail pairs with nothing on the template in the first cycles.
expected: One band at 2629 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Drop the annealing temperature by 3 °C and check the pUC19 template is there.
Raise the annealing temperature, or gel-purify the band of the right size.

steps.title: Amplify GFP
instructions: Thaw the buffer, dNTPs and primers on ice, then vortex and spin them down.
Mix the master mix, dispense it into each tube, then add the GFP template.
Run the program below: 63 °C annealing and 20 s extension for a 749 bp product.
notes: Its 5' tails are 16 bp of pUC19 backbone on the forward primer and 16 bp of pUC19 backbone on the reverse primer, so the amplicon already spells what its neighbours spell where they meet.
The annealing temperature above is read from the annealing regions alone; a tail pairs with nothing on the template in the first cycles.
expected: One band at 749 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Drop the annealing temperature by 3 °C and check the GFP template is there.
Raise the annealing temperature, or gel-purify the band of the right size.

steps.title: Check the PCRs on a gel
instructions: Use a 1% agarose gel.
Load 5 µL of each reaction beside the ladder.
Run until the dye front is two thirds down the gel.

notes.text: 1% agarose resolves bands of these sizes.

expected: pUC19 backbone: one band at 2629 bp.
GFP: one band at 749 bp.

troubleshooting.problem: A smear or an extra band
troubleshooting.solution: Gel-purify the band of the right size; a wrong template in the assembly gives wrong clones.

steps.title: Digest the plasmid template with DpnI
instructions: Add 20 units of DpnI to the pUC19 backbone PCR and mix.
Incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Heat-inactivate DpnI at 80 °C for 20 minutes.

notes.text: DpnI cuts GATC only where Dam has methylated it, so it cuts pUC19 (15 Dam sites) and leaves the PCR product, which carries no methylation.
The dose, the time and the heat inactivation are the assembly manual's, not this package's.
The other answer to template background is to keep it low in the first place: 0.1-0.5 ng of plasmid per 50 µL PCR.

expected: Nothing visible. The digest shows up later as fewer colonies carrying the template plasmid.

troubleshooting.problem: Many colonies on the no-insert control
troubleshooting.solution: The template survived: digest longer, or use more DpnI.

steps.title: Purify every amplicon
instructions: Run each reaction over a Monarch Spin PCR & DNA Cleanup column and elute in the smallest volume the kit allows.

notes.text: A column is optional below 3 PCR fragments: a product more than 90% pure goes into the reaction unpurified, within the fraction the assembly step gives.

At 3 fragments or more, or a fragment over 5 kb, a column is highly recommended, and the gain in assembly and transformation is put at two- to tenfold. A PCR showing anything but one band is gel-purified whatever the count.

expected: Clean DNA, free of polymerase, primers and dNTPs.

troubleshooting.solution: Elute in a larger volume and leave the buffer on the column longer.

steps.title: Measure every concentration
instructions: Measure each purified amplicon by A260 (NanoDrop) or with a fluorometer (Qubit).
Enter each concentration in the next table's Stock column.
expected: pUC19 backbone: 0.0309 pmol is 50.04 ng, so 50 ng/µL or more fits in 1 µL.
GFP: 0.0618 pmol is 27.29 ng, so 27 ng/µL or more fits in 1 µL.

troubleshooting.problem: Too dilute to fit in the reaction
troubleshooting.solution: Concentrate the amplicon, or scale the reaction up.

steps.title: Set up the NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix reaction
instructions: Thaw the master mix on ice and mix it well.
Pipette the DNA into the tube first, then the master mix.
Mix gently and spin down.

notes.text: Each insert goes in at 2 times the vector's moles, and any insert under 200 bp at 5 times, at this fragment count. The table gives each in picomoles and in nanograms, so it can be pipetted at whatever concentration it is.
Unpurified PCR product goes straight from the tube for up to 20% of the reaction, which is 4 µL here, as long as the product is a single band.

components.name: NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix

tables.title: NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix reaction

expected: A 20 µL reaction holding every fragment.

troubleshooting.problem: The DNA does not fit the reaction volume
troubleshooting.solution: Concentrate the fragments, or scale the whole reaction up and add master mix in proportion.

troubleshooting.problem: Colonies later carry the empty vector
troubleshooting.solution: The backbone PCR carried its plasmid template through; digest it with DpnI again, or gel-purify the backbone.

steps.title: Incubate the assembly
instructions: Put the tube in the thermocycler and run the program below.
Put the reaction on ice afterwards, or keep it at -20 °C.

notes.text: 15 minutes is what this fragment count takes. Incubating longer than 15 minutes improves some assemblies, up to four hours; overnight is refused.

notes: Junction positions are 1-based, on the product.

figures.caption: pUC19-GFP as the incubation closes it: the overlaps the parts share, 16 bp and 16 bp.

expected: Nothing visible. One exonuclease, one polymerase and one ligase work together at this one temperature; there is nothing to cycle.
The product spells TAAAACGACGGCCAGT at 380, where pUC19 backbone meets GFP.
The product spells GGCGTAATCATGGTCA at 1113, where GFP meets pUC19 backbone.

troubleshooting.solution: Run the kit's positive control beside the assembly; it tells a bad master mix from a bad design.
Run the reaction on a gel: an efficient assembly shows the fragments gone and a product of the right size.

steps.title: Transform and plate
instructions: Thaw 50 µL of NEB 5-alpha Competent E. coli (C2987) on ice for 10 minutes.
Add 2 µL of the assembly and flick the tube four or five times.
Hold on ice for 30 minutes.
Heat shock at 42 °C for 30 seconds.
Return to ice for 5 minutes.
Add 950 µL of outgrowth medium and shake at 37 °C for 60 minutes at 250 rpm.
Spread 50 µL of a 1:5 dilution on a warmed plate and grow overnight at 37 °C.
cautions: Competent cells die if they warm up; keep them on ice until the shock.
notes: The plate reads colour only with an alpha-complementing host, such as NEB 5-alpha Competent E. coli (C2987). A host that cannot complement gives white colonies whatever the clone carries.
The clone is not expected to make GFP: it reads on the opposite strand from lac promoter and no ribosome binding site is annotated ahead of it.
expected: Hundreds of colonies. NEB's own lot test asks for more than 100 from a six-fragment assembly with a tenth of the outgrowth plated; this reaction joins 2.
Correct clones are white and empty vector is blue: the insertion interrupts lacZα, which is then not there to complete the host's own.

troubleshooting.solution: Check the antibiotic and the cells' efficiency, and plate the rest of the outgrowth.
Plate a smaller volume or a greater dilution next time.

steps.title: Screen colonies by PCR
instructions: Touch a well-separated colony with a sterile toothpick and stir it into the tube until the liquid clouds.
Streak the same toothpick onto a numbered plate, so the clone survives the PCR.
Run the program below and load 5 µL on a 2% gel.
notes: The long first step at 94 °C lyses the cells; there is no purified template.

notes.text: The correct fraction falls with fragment count: 10 of 10 correct at two fragments, 4 of 10 at five. That is the In-Fusion series' number, the only one measured against fragment count, and not this product's.

components.name: OneTaq Quick-Load 2X Master Mix with Standard Buffer (M0486)

expected: Each of the 2 junctions is read: the flanking pair crosses them all, and each junction primer stops inside its own insert.
Correct clone: 160 bp, 837 bp.
Empty vector: 177 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: The colony was too much material: touch a smaller one, or dilute it.
Run the same PCR on the assembly reaction itself, with primers flanking the assembled product.

troubleshooting.problem: Every colony reads as empty vector
troubleshooting.solution: A PCR-generated vector carries uncut plasmid through; digest it with DpnI again, or gel-purify the backbone.

troubleshooting.problem: A colony gives a band of the wrong size
troubleshooting.solution: The PCR that made a part was not a single band; gel-purify it and assemble again. NEB Stable Competent E. coli (#C3040) suits an insert carrying repeats.

steps.title: Confirm the clone by sequencing
instructions: Miniprep two or three colonies that read as correct.
Send each miniprep with both sequencing primers.
Check the read across every junction and the whole of each insert.
notes: Only a read across the junctions confirms the assembly, whatever the screen said.
A provider whose read is shorter than the lengths above needs a further primer inside the inserts.

notes.text: About one error per 50 molecules joined was found in 210 sequenced junctions, so a gel that reads right is not the same as a junction that is right.

expected: Sequencing forward anneals 123 bp from its own junction and has to read 840 bp to cover the far one.
Sequencing reverse anneals 118 bp from its own junction and has to read 835 bp to cover the far one.
The junctions read as TAAAACGACGGCCAGT and GGCGTAATCATGGTCA, and the parts match GFP.

troubleshooting.problem: The read starts too close to the junction
troubleshooting.solution: Move the primer further out; the first bases after a primer are unreadable.
